semantics.requirement: Return every department, including departments with zero employees, with employee count.

alternatives.sql: SELECT d.id AS department_id, d.name AS department_name, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count FROM department d LEFT JOIN employee e ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id, d.name
SELECT d.id AS department_id, d.name AS department_name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employee e WHERE e.department_id = d.id) AS employee_count FROM department d

semantics.requirement: Count only rows whose email is non-NULL.

alternatives.sql: SELECT COUNT(email) AS non_null_email_count FROM customer
SELECT COUNT(*) AS non_null_email_count FROM customer WHERE email IS NOT NULL

semantics.requirement: Return customers that have no matching order.

alternatives.sql: SELECT c.id AS customer_id FROM customer c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id)
SELECT c.id AS customer_id FROM customer c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL

semantics.requirement: Return customers whose total non-NULL order amount exceeds 100.

alternatives.sql: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount) > 100
SELECT c.id AS customer_id, x.total_amount FROM customer c JOIN (SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) x ON x.customer_id = c.id WHERE x.total_amount > 100
SELECT DISTINCT city FROM customer WHERE city IS NOT NULL ORDER BY city ASC
SELECT city FROM customer WHERE city IS NOT NULL GROUP BY city ORDER BY city ASC
